item.title: Seven Orange Tabby Kittens Found Under a Fallen Tree at a Senior Home Are a Happy Challenge to Tell Apart
item.description:
A mama cat and her seven tiny kittens were found living under a fallen tree at a senior living facility in Indianapolis, and a rescue team reached them within fifteen minutes of the call. Now safe and warm in foster care, the whole family has been christened the Golden Years Gang, each one named after a grandparent.

Millie and her babiesCredit: Lori White

Their rescue began with a call for help. Word came in about a mother cat and her seven little ones who had been getting by beneath a fallen tree at a senior living facility on the south side of Indianapolis. It was no place for a family of eight.

When a rescuer with Alliance for Responsible Pet Ownership, a foster-based rescue in Indianapolis, arrived and surveyed the scene, there was no saying no. She got straight on the phone.

The response was immediate. "We couldn't say no to helping them, so we quickly made some calls, and within 15 minutes my husband and daughter arrived with old towels, Churus, and carriers," Lori White, the ARPO foster now caring for the family, shared with LoveMeow.

The rescue Credit: Lori White

With old towels for warmth, Churu treats to coax the cats out, and carriers ready to go, the little team gathered up the whole family in one swift, careful effort.

Momma and all seven babies were carried away from the outdoors for good. It was the kind of day that leaves a rescuer grateful for the friends and family who show up without hesitation when a family of cats needs them most.

LoveMeow may earn a small commission from purchases made through links in this article at no additional cost to you.

Tucked into the hollowCredit: Lori White

Once they were safe, the little family inspired a naming theme as charming as the rescue itself. Lori thought it over through the rest of the evening, and by the time she had washed the rescue dirt out of her hair, she had landed on a Golden Years Gang theme, a nod to the senior living facility where the family had been found. Each cat got a wonderfully old-fashioned name to match.

At the head of the family is Momma Mildred, Millie for short. Her seven kittens are five boys, Norman, Stanley, Bernard, Eugene, and Otis Henry, and two little girls, Dottie and Pearl Louise.

The whole boy gangCredit: Lori White

The kittens are only about two and a half to three weeks old, tiny and precious, and just beginning to explore the world from the safety of their foster home.

Telling all those little faces apart has become a happy challenge. "Five ginger boys with matching baby faces did not get the memo about making my job easier," Lori shared with us. Even so, a system has emerged: Stanley is the lone blondie, big Bernard is the largest and darkest of the brothers, and little Norman, the smallest, has the long fur that gives him away.

Sound asleep togetherCredit: Lori White

And Momma Millie is flourishing. After going without proper nutrition while living outdoors, she is eating with real gusto. "We have no doubt she is trying to make up for all the nutrients she wasn't getting while living outdoors," Lori shared.

She is pouring all of it back into her babies, and it shows in every content, well-fed kitten curled up against her. She is being a Mom, by every measure, in every part of the word.

Sweet dreams Credit: Lori White

Now that they are indoors, the whole family is enjoying the small comforts they went so long without. They are safe, they are warm, their bellies are full, and they are wrapped in the attention they missed for so long.

For a mama who worked so hard to keep her babies alive against the elements, it is an enormous relief. She can finally rest, knowing her family is in good hands.

One big cuddle puddle Credit: Lori White

Not long ago, Millie was raising seven kittens alone beneath a fallen tree, doing everything she could to keep them warm and fed. Now the whole Golden Years Gang is indoors, full-bellied and safe, with nothing left to do but grow up surrounded by love.

For a family that started with nothing but each other, it is the softest of landings, and the best of their story is still ahead.

Mama MillieCredit: Lori White

Share this story with your friends. View more on Millie and her Golden Years Gang journey with Lori White on Instagram @dreaming_of_foster_kittens, and learn more about ARPO at arporescue.org.

item.title: Cat Passed From Home to Home Was Reunited With His Rescue by a Microchip, and Now Holds Hands When Pet
item.description:
A gray cat who moved from home to home for years is reunited with his original rescue thanks to a kind woman and his microchip. Now he holds hands with whoever gives him sweet pets.

Truly ScrumptiousCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

Truly Scrumptious, or Truly for short, is a sweet four-year-old gray cat whose story began happily enough. He was adopted as a kitten in 2022 from Whiskers-A-GoGo, an all-volunteer cat rescue in Brooklyn, and sent off with every hope for a wonderful life.

The years that followed took some hard turns. About a year after the adoption, the woman who took him home split with her boyfriend, and he kept the cat, even though she had signed the adoption papers. A few years later, he moved to an apartment that did not allow pets and left Truly with his elderly mother.

item.title: Bonded Kittens From a Packed Shelter Now Spend Their Nights Watching True Crime, Unbothered by a Plot Twist
item.description:
Two bonded kitten siblings were pulled from a crowded shelter and landed somewhere far cozier. Now their favorite way to spend an evening is stretched out along the back of the couch, quietly watching true crime documentaries with their foster.

Mahi Mahi and MackerelCredit: Orphan Kitten Project

Mahi Mahi and Mackerel came into rescue after a local shelter, packed well past its comfortable limit, put out a call for help. With so many animals arriving at once, the shelter hoped to find these two a softer place to land, and reached out to ask whether any foster homes might be open.

That call reached Orphan Kitten Project, a vet student-run rescue at UC Davis, California, that runs entirely on foster homes and has no shelter building of its own. "We are 100% foster-based, so we do not have a shelter facility. When we take in kittens, they are always placed in a foster home," Orphan Kitten Project shared with LoveMeow.

For a group that loves nothing more than getting kittens out of crowded shelters and into real homes, the answer was an easy yes. The two siblings were placed with a devoted foster, and in her care they settled in and began to blossom.

Mellow to the coreCredit: Orphan Kitten Project

Mahi Mahi and Mackerel turned out to be the most wonderfully easygoing pair. They are sweet, mellow, and delightfully low-key, the kind of kittens who bring a calm presence into a room, and they seldom meow, choosing instead to gaze up with big eyes when they would like to be scooped up for a cuddle.

Their foster calls them easy keepers, content to entertain themselves for hours. "They are not destructive or demanding, and can keep themselves entertained as long as they are supplied with a scratcher and each other," the rescue shared. That last part matters most, because their bond sits at the very center of who they are.

Favorite toyCredit: Orphan Kitten Project

Their laid-back charm is only half the story. Hand either of them a wand toy or a bouncy spring, and the calm gives way to a lively chase, all pounces and skittering paws across the floor.

When the game winds down, they melt into whoever is holding them, easy to pick up and glad to be held. Watching the two of them tear around and then flop into a lap, it is clear these are kittens who feel completely at home.

[VIDEO — Mahi Mahi and Mackerel at play: editor to embed] Caption: Playtime

Bonded gray tabby kittens playing with toy | LoveMeow Credit: Orphan Kitten Project

Their gentle manners have won over everyone they meet. Neither one plays rough, and they do not scratch or bite, which makes them as easy to live with as they are to look at. They get along beautifully with other cats, too.

That easygoing streak runs deep. "They have also proven to be good with high-energy kids and high-energy yappy dogs," the rescue shared, the kind of pair who take a noisy, busy household in stride.

Taking it all in strideCredit: Orphan Kitten Project

New and startling things barely faze them either. Even the vacuum cleaner earns no more than a moment's pause before the two return to their contented selves.

The detail that truly wins people over, though, comes in the evenings. When the day slows down, Mahi Mahi and Mackerel like to stretch out along the high back of the couch, curled close together, keeping their foster company through a true crime documentary or two.

Come back hereCredit: Orphan Kitten Project

Lined up along the top of the cushions, calm and unbothered, they turn an ordinary night on the couch into their favorite part of the day.

It is a small, cozy ritual, and a long way from the crowded shelter where they started. Mahi Mahi and Mackerel are a bonded pair and will be adopted together.

Ready for a couch of their ownCredit: Orphan Kitten Project

Mahi Mahi and Mackerel started as two more kittens in a shelter with more animals than room. Now they are an easygoing pair with a favorite spot on the back of the couch, and a whole evening of documentaries waiting for the family who will watch along.
